name: Almost Ready Temporary Page
author: Jos Velasco

sections.description:
Almost Ready Temporary Page is a simple plugin that shows a friendly temporary page to visitors while you work on your WordPress site. Unlike other plugins, it uses native WordPress core blocks — no custom builders or proprietary templates required.

What it does:

  • Creates a simple temporary page automatically when activated
  • Shows this page to all website visitors
  • Lets you and other logged-in users access the site normally to keep working
  • Uses your theme’s styling so it looks consistent with your brand
  • Completely customizable using WordPress’s native block editor

Key Features:

  • Native Blocks – Uses WordPress core blocks, no proprietary builders
  • Automatic Setup – No complicated configuration needed
  • Smart Detection – Visitors see the temporary page, logged-in users see the normal site
  • Fully Customizable – Change text, colors, layout, add images using blocks
  • Settings Page – Activate/deactivate and assign any page directly from Settings > Almost Ready
  • Rename Freely – Rename the page title and slug without breaking anything — the plugin tracks it by ID
  • SEO Friendly – Tells search engines not to index the temporary page
  • Private Content – Visitors can’t read your posts and pages through the REST API while the temporary page is active
  • Theme Compatible – Works with any WordPress theme
  • Clean Removal – When deactivated, everything returns to normal
  • Clean Uninstall – Optionally delete all plugin data when uninstalling (the page itself is kept)

Perfect for:

  • Website updates and maintenance
  • Launching new websites while still working on them
  • Making design changes without visitors seeing work-in-progress
  • Temporary downtime periods
  • Any time you need privacy while working on your site
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/almost-ready-temporary-page or install through WordPress admin
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen
  3. That’s it! The temporary page is now live for visitors
  4. To customize the page, go to Pages > All Pages and edit “Almost Ready”
  5. To manage settings, go to Settings > Almost Ready
sections.faq:
How do I customize the temporary page?

Go to Pages > All Pages in your WordPress admin and click “Edit” on the page labeled “Temporary Page” (“Almost Ready” unless you renamed it or chose another). It’s a regular page edited in the block editor, not a template in the Site Editor. You can change the text, add images, modify colors, and rearrange the layout using the block editor – just like editing any other page.

Can I preview what visitors see?

Yes! Either log out of WordPress or open a private/incognito browser window to see exactly what your visitors see.

Will this affect my website permanently?

Not at all. When you deactivate the plugin or turn the temporary page off, your website returns to normal immediately. The default “Almost Ready” page is saved as a draft but isn’t deleted, so you can turn it back on anytime. If you chose one of your own pages instead, it becomes a regular page again. It is only set back to draft if it was a draft that the plugin published.

Can I still access my admin area?

Absolutely. You and anyone else who is logged in can access everything normally – the admin area, your regular pages, everything. Only visitors who aren’t logged in see the temporary page.

What about search engines?

The plugin tells search engines not to index the temporary page, so it won’t hurt your SEO. When you deactivate the plugin or turn the temporary page off, your normal site pages will be crawled again.

Do I need to know any code?

Nope! Everything works automatically. If you want to customize the page, you can do it through the familiar WordPress page editor without touching any code.

Can I rename the temporary page?

Yes! You can rename the page title and slug to anything you like. The plugin tracks the page by its ID, not its slug, so renaming it won’t break anything.

Can I use an existing page instead of the one the plugin created?

Yes. Go to Settings > Almost Ready and select any page from the dropdown.

Will the plugin delete my page if I uninstall it?

No. The temporary page is always kept. If you want the plugin to also remove its data from the database on uninstall, enable “Delete plugin data when uninstalling” in Settings > Almost Ready before deleting the plugin.

Does it block the REST API?

Yes. While the temporary page is active, visitors who aren’t logged in get an error from the REST API (/wp-json/), so they can’t read your content that way either. The block editor and anything you do while logged in keep working.

If a plugin needs a REST route for visitors, such as a contact form on the temporary page, you can open its route with a filter:

add_filter( 'artp_rest_allowed_routes', function ( $routes ) {
    $routes[] = '/contact-form-7/v1';
    return $routes;
} );

What happens to the old page when I choose a different one?

If you switch away from the default “Almost Ready” page the plugin created, it is set to draft so it doesn’t stay public. A page you chose yourself keeps its status, because it may have real content, both when you switch pages and when you turn the temporary page off. The exception is a draft that the plugin published for you: it goes back to draft. Nothing is deleted.

What makes this different from other maintenance plugins?

Almost Ready Temporary Page is the only plugin that uses native WordPress core blocks for the temporary page. Other plugins use custom builders or proprietary templates. This means your page is lightweight, future-proof, and works exactly like any other WordPress page.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: The REST API is blocked for visitors while the temporary page is active, so posts and pages can’t be read through /wp-json/. Use the artp_rest_allowed_routes filter to open specific routes.
  • New: The redirect and the temporary page send no-cache headers, so browsers and proxies don’t keep showing them after you turn the mode off.
  • New: The temporary page is labeled “Temporary Page” in the Pages list, like the front page and privacy policy page.
  • New: The “Page Options” menu in the admin notice links to Settings.
  • Fix: Choosing a different page in Settings now sets the default “Almost Ready” page to draft instead of leaving it published.
  • Change: Turning the temporary page off, or switching away from it, no longer unpublishes a page you chose yourself, unless it was a draft the plugin published. The default “Almost Ready” page still goes to draft. On/off is now stored as its own setting; existing sites keep their current state.
  • Removed the manual textdomain loading; WordPress.org language packs load automatically.

1.1.3

  • Fix: On WordPress 7.2 and later, random content redirects (/random/, ?random) sent visitors to real post URLs before the temporary page, revealing their addresses. Visitors now go straight to the temporary page.

1.1.2

  • Fix: Plugin textdomain was never loaded, preventing translations from being applied
  • Removed incomplete bundled es_ES translation in favour of community translations on translate.wordpress.org

1.1.1

  • Fix: /login and /admin URL shortcuts now correctly redirect to wp-login.php when the temporary page is active
  • Props @pmmueller for the report

1.1.0

  • Added Settings page under Settings > Almost Ready
  • Activate/deactivate the temporary page from the Settings page
  • Assign any existing page as the temporary page via a dropdown
  • Pages are now tracked by ID instead of slug — renaming the page title or slug is fully supported
  • Plugin row link switches to Settings when the temporary page is inactive
  • Added “Delete plugin data when uninstalling” option (the temporary page itself is always kept)
  • Existing installs are migrated automatically
  • Props @pmmueller for suggesting the ability to rename the temporary page

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Automatic temporary page creation
  • Native block editor customization
  • SEO-friendly noindex tags
  • Smart user detection
